technical_and_design_decisions: Implement Sqoop metastore selection through externalized configuration, preserving the current default for backward compatibility and delegating connection details to the existing supported persistence mechanism.

Expose metrics collection endpoints using REST paths for all counters, gauges, and rich-gauges, returning a single structured JSON document per metric type while preserving existing individual-metric endpoints.

Implement the Boot-based ModuleRunner as a Spring Boot application component that can run without xd-containers and supports container-managed lifecycle, configuration, logging, and graceful shutdown.
Use the existing GemFire source integration and add documented native GemFire authentication and security property configuration rather than introducing a new security abstraction.
Implement jdbcgpfdist as a batch-oriented job that reuses the existing gpfdist sink/writer behavior and adds JDBC reader, job configuration, restart/error handling, and schema mapping.
Separate repository-backed test fixtures from mock-based tests through explicit test support interfaces and independently selectable test configurations.
Move the Reactor data processor module into the core repository/module structure while preserving its public processor contract and using the supported Reactor Stream API.
Follow the project's existing Java, Spring, build, dependency-injection, logging, testing, REST, and documentation conventions wherever the specification is silent.
assumptions: The increment is implemented in an existing Spring XD-style multi-module Java repository with a functioning build, CI setup, and existing implementations for Sqoop, metrics, GemFire, gpfdist, batch processing, testing infrastructure, and Reactor integration.
No major framework upgrade, database migration, UI work, or backward-incompatible API redesign is required.
U1 requires configuration of an alternate Sqoop metastore database using existing supported JDBC or metastore abstractions; implementation of new database drivers is excluded.
U2 is limited to authoring and integrating configuration documentation for an HDFS-backed module registry; the underlying registry implementation already exists.

U3 requires the three specified collection endpoints and JSON serialization of all currently registered metrics; pagination, filtering, aggregation, authentication changes, and dashboard UI are excluded.

U4 covers a minimally production-usable Boot-based ModuleRunner, including configuration, lifecycle management, packaging, and representative container execution support; full orchestration-platform integration is excluded.
U5 assumes the existing GemFire source can consume native GemFire authentication through configured properties and that no new GemFire server-side security implementation is needed.
U6 assumes existing JDBC batch reader and job infrastructure can be reused, and that gpfdist protocol behavior is already implemented by the existing sink.
U7 includes refactoring and representative migration of the existing test suite, but not rewriting every test or replacing the repository technology.

U8 includes moving and adapting the existing Reactor processor module, dependency and package updates, regression tests, and documentation; new Reactor operators or unrelated processor features are excluded.
Estimates include implementation, code review preparation, unit/integration testing, documentation, and local validation by one developer, but exclude waiting time for external teams or environments.
All estimates are work-hours and represent most likely effort rather than elapsed calendar duration.

activities.activity_description: Inspect existing modules, build conventions, relevant implementations, APIs, test infrastructure, configuration patterns, and dependency constraints; produce an implementation plan covering all eight user stories.

Add externalized metastore selection and connection configuration, preserve default behavior, integrate with application startup and configuration binding, and handle invalid or incomplete configuration.
Add unit and integration coverage for default and alternate metastore configurations, perform compatibility checks, and document configuration examples and operational behavior.
Document the required HDFS-backed module registry properties, recommended configuration, deployment considerations, examples, and troubleshooting guidance.

Design and implement the counters/all, gauges/all, and rich-gauges/all endpoints, including routing, service-layer retrieval, response DTOs, serialization, and compatibility with existing metrics endpoints.
Add controller, service, serialization, empty-result, error, and regression tests for all three aggregate metrics endpoints.
Document endpoint paths, response formats, examples, metric naming behavior, and operational considerations for custom dashboard clients.

Create the Boot-based runner, integrate module loading and execution, support externalized configuration and container-managed lifecycle, provide packaging and startup behavior, and implement graceful shutdown.
Add unit and integration tests for startup, configuration, module execution, failure handling, shutdown, and representative container-style execution.
Document usage, configuration, packaging, container invocation, lifecycle behavior, logging, and migration from xd-containers.
Integrate native GemFire authentication and security properties into the GemFire source configuration path, including property binding, propagation, validation, and secure handling of credentials.
Add tests for authenticated and unauthenticated configurations, property propagation, invalid credentials or settings, and preservation of unsecured default behavior where applicable.
Document GemFire native and security-specific properties, placement of configuration, credential considerations, and secured source setup examples.

Create the out-of-the-box JDBC-to-gpfdist batch job, configure JDBC reading and mapping, adapt the existing gpfdist writer for batch execution, and integrate job parameters, error handling, and restart semantics.
Add unit and integration tests using representative JDBC data, validate gpfdist output behavior, cover mappings and failures, and verify batch lifecycle and restart behavior.
Document job configuration, JDBC connection properties, table/query and mapping options, gpfdist destination settings, examples, limitations, and operational usage.
Refactor test support so mock dependencies and real repository integrations are separately configured and coupled through thin interfaces or fixtures, while preserving existing test execution modes.
Migrate representative affected tests, add mock-only and repository-backed execution coverage, update build profiles, and validate isolation and repeatability.

Move the Reactor data processor module into the core repository structure, update packages and build dependencies, preserve module metadata and public contracts, and expose native Reactor Stream API usage.
Adapt and expand processor tests, verify stream composition and runtime behavior, validate compatibility with existing module execution, and update representative examples.
Document the new module location, dependency and usage model, supported Reactor Stream patterns, configuration, and migration guidance.
Run full builds, dependency checks, static analysis, focused integration environments, backward-compatibility checks, packaging validation, and resolve cross-story integration defects.
Perform final code cleanup, review configuration and documentation consistency, update release notes or migration notes, and prepare the completed increment for CI and handoff.
